commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Move user message construction from Neil
commitResults.messageBody:
Neil constructs user-facing messages, mixing application coordination
with presentation concerns.

Move task-related message formatting into Ui so Neil focuses on
coordinating application logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Set Neil as application main class
Test: Add coverage for core task logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Task parsing, list management, and storage are core workflows with
limited automated coverage. Regressions in these paths can reach users
without early feedback.

Add JUnit tests for task state and decoding, parser validation, list
operations, and persistence. Document a target of testing the
highest-value 50% of methods and updating tests alongside code changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword search for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need a quick way to locate tasks without scanning the entire list.

Add a find command that searches task descriptions case-insensitively,
preserves result order, and rejects commands without a search term.

Add tests for parsing, matching, result ordering, and UI output.

The project relies on manual review to enforce Java coding style.

Style violations can therefore be missed or applied inconsistently.

Let's add the SE-EDU Checkstyle rules to Gradle and verify production
and test code as part of the standard check lifecycle.

Update existing test formatting so the codebase passes the new checks.

Neil accepts commands only through terminal input, which limits the
application to a CLI workflow.

Add an FXML-based chatbot window that displays user commands and Neil's
responses as dialog bubbles. Route commands through the existing parser,
task list, and storage logic so behavior and persistence remain unchanged.

Configure Gradle with JavaFX and make the GUI the application entry point.
Close the application when the user enters `bye`, matching the CLI exit
behavior. Add tests for command responses and persistence.
